To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of pulses as input to the classifier outperforms the complete song as input, that the use of a larger number of classes (species) degrades performance, and that the best performance is achieved when the number of classes is small (up to 10).
the use of short audio segments of bird songs (pulses) improves the identification accuracy and that the identification of bird species is feasible with a high number of classes (more than 200).
the identification accuracy increases with the number of classes and that the best results are obtained when using pulses instead of the complete signal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic identification of the bird species from their recorded song.
the development of a complete automatic system to recognize bird species using audio recordings.
the development of a methodology to automatically identify the species of a bird from its recorded song, using machine learning techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a bird species can be correctly identified with a high degree of certainty if the audio signal contains at least one of its typical song pulses, even when the signal is noisy and the species is not previously known.
the identification accuracy of a bird song is directly related to the number of species present in the training set.
the best results are obtained with the pulses (short audio signals) for a large number of bird species, while the complete audio signal performs better in a reduced number of bird species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the identification accuracy of bird species using our method is high enough to be used in practical applications.
we have developed a complete automatic procedure for bird species identification.
the bird song classification accuracy increases with the number of classes and the best performance is obtained using pulses as input.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the bird identification can be done in a reliable way using a small amount of audio data, and that the identification performance does not depend strongly on the number of bird species in the problem.

the use of pulses instead of the complete audio signals is more effective in terms of classification accuracy, and the use of a large number of classes (species) does not degrade the classification performance, as it is usually expected.

the use of the pulse segments instead of the complete song signals improves the accuracy of the identification process, and that this improvement is independent of the number of bird species in the dataset.
